text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The elders council of Namibia's ruling SWAPO party has urged President Sam Nujoma to stand for a third term as head of state. General Secretary Kanana Hishoono said the President was still medically fit to continue with his duties.

- An investigation by the police into a suspected multi-million dollar smuggling and bribery case, allegedly involving customs officials and a Namibian clothing company, is expected to be finalised soon.
- Norway apparently plans to close its embassies in Namibia and Botswana with diplomatic work between the two states and the Nordic country to be transferred to Pretoria.
- The Ministry of Works, Transport and Communication has launched a campaign for further improvement of aviation safety in Namibia.
- The Haib copper project could be realised by September this year bringing one of the biggest investments ever to Namibia, said Peter Prentice of Australian mining company Great Fitzroy Mines.
